name: tray
title: A tray printed flat that folds up: four walls on arrays of LET joints
orientation: Flat on the bed as drawn at fold 0, one piece, no supports. Fold each wall up by hand: its four joints share the turn.

tray.label: The tray: base, four walls and their joints in one print

base.rule: The base's side, a square; each wall is as long as its edge. Each edge's joints take 12.36 mm of it, and two edges' joints must not meet at a corner: 60 leaves 35.28 mm between the bands, over the joints' 30 and their 0.5 mm laps

wall.rule: Each wall's height flat, from the base's edge: half of it goes into the joints' band, so a wall stands about 10 mm above the joints

thickness.rule: The sheet: six layers, so the torsion bars are as deep as they are wide and a half

joint_w.rule: Each LET joint's length along its edge: longer bars twist further for a strain

bar.rule: A torsion bar's width: two lines, the thinnest wall that prints solid

slot.rule: The slots' width: over the printer's 0.3 mm gap, so the bars print free of each other

bridge.rule: The bridges' width along the edge

series.rule: Joints in series across each fold: four share 90 degrees at 22.5 each, about half the 43.4 degrees PETG's strain limit allows one (1.93 times the margin)

fold.rule: The walls' fold as drawn: 0 as printed; an assembly's pose sets 90 to show them standing

folded.rule: The fold the tray is checked to: the walls standing

clearance.rule: The least gap between two rigid parts on the way from flat to standing
